instruction: Create an animated GIF file named video_clip.gif from the video file src.mp4 on the desktop, extracting a 5-second segment that starts at the 2-second mark.

metadata.explanation: Task requires using VLC and GIMP to create an animated GIF from a video file. Agent must: 1) Open video in VLC, 2) Navigate to 2-second mark, 3) Extract/record 5-second clip, 4) Import frames to GIMP, 5) Export as animated GIF. Evaluator checks file exists, is GIF format, and has multiple frames (at least 10) indicating animation.

scoring_breakdown.0.5: GIF file exists at specified location

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file existence at the specified path (/home/user/Desktop/video_clip.gif)
Evaluator correctly verifies GIF format using PIL image analysis
Evaluator correctly verifies animation by counting frames (checks frame_count >= 10)
Getter logic is sound: downloads file from VM, uses PIL to analyze format and count frames
INCOMPLETE: Instruction requires '5-second segment starting at 2 seconds', but evaluator does not verify duration (only checks frame count)
INCOMPLETE: No verification that the GIF content actually corresponds to the 2-7 second segment of the source video

WEAK THRESHOLD: min_frames=10 is unreasonably low for a 5-second video segment. At standard frame rates (24-30 fps), a 5-second clip should have 120-150 frames. A 10-frame GIF would be ~2 fps, more like a slideshow than a video conversion
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Increase min_frames threshold to a more realistic value for 5-second video (e.g., 100-120 frames minimum, assuming 20-24 fps)
Optionally: Add duration verification by calculating expected duration from frame_count and typical GIF frame delays

Note: Content verification (verifying the GIF shows frames from 2-7 seconds of source video) is technically very difficult without video analysis, so omitting this is acceptable for practical purposes
